families.family_description: OH-rich biopolymer matrices combined with retained acid-like phases and optional film formers aim to preserve flexible hydrogen-bonded proton pathways in the cold window.
descriptor_match: D2: DES or bound polar phases are reported to maintain plasticised conducting continuity in chitosan systems.
D3: polysaccharide-rich hosts are analogously flexible when plasticised rather than left as dry brittle films.
D4: phosphoric-acid DES motifs provide non-crystallising acid speciation under confinement.
D6: starch, PVA, and related OH-rich hosts supply dense donor/acceptor sites.
D7: chitosan and low-doped phosphoric-acid biopolymer systems show conducting-phase retention.

families.family_description: One-dimensional tubular or fibrous mineral hosts combined with polymeric binders and proton carriers can create retained nanoconfined transport channels that resist cold-phase disruption.
descriptor_match: D5: attapulgite, halloysite, and carbon-dot-organised composites support interconnected confinement.
D6: phosphoric acid and heteropolyacid species provide proton-relay functionality within confined networks.
D7: attapulgite and halloysite are reported to reduce acid loss or immobilise the conducting phase.
D1: low-temperature PA composite evidence supports continuity down to subzero conditions by analogy.

families.family_description: Protonated phosphate-rich amorphous networks offer intrinsically continuous transport media with strong hydrogen-bonding and retained proton species, optionally hybridised with softer hosts.
descriptor_match: D1: protonated phosphate glass is directly described as an amorphous continuous proton-transport medium.
D4: proton-rich phosphate networks are analogs for cold-stable non-crystallising acid form under confinement.
D6: phosphate glass provides strong hydrogen-bond-mediated proton mobility.
D7: the proton species are structurally retained within the amorphous network, though humidity dependence is a risk.

instances.composition_description: A quaternary membrane using chitosan as the primary biopolymer host, PVA as a film-forming OH-rich flexibiliser, attapulgite as a 1-D confining filler, and retained phosphoric acid as the proton source.
expected_properties: cold_window: plausible bound-water and acid continuity from OH-rich host plus retained acid
nanoconfinement: 1-D filler should guide interconnected proton channels
retention: clay-biopolymer interactions may suppress phosphoric-acid loss
risk_flags: PA leaching if acid loading is too high
subzero brittleness if plasticisation is insufficient

element_evidence.reason: Chitosan is reported as an acid-interacting scaffold with retention capacity, making it a plausible cold-operable host when plasticised.
PVA contributes dense OH-mediated hydrogen bonding and acts as an analogous flexible film-former in polysaccharide blends.
1-D attapulgite is directly linked to channel guidance and acid immobilisation in composite proton-conducting membranes.
Phosphoric acid is evidenced as a proton-conducting acid phase and is more cold-stable when complexed or confined rather than used as a bulk phase.

instances.novelty_rationale: This combines the requested quaternary synergy motifs into one cold-side-targeted membrane archetype. The individual roles are evidenced, but this exact four-component formulation is not directly present in the pool.

instances.composition_description: A starch/PVA blended film plasticised by a choline chloride–phosphoric acid deep eutectic to provide a non-crystallising proton-conducting phase.
expected_properties: cold_window: DES-like phase may avoid freezing-like disruption near 200 K better than free water
matrix_flexibility: starch/PVA hydrogen bonding should support a cohesive plasticised film
proton_relay: acid plus OH-rich matrix offers hybrid vehicular and hopping pathways
risk_flags: excess DES may weaken mechanical integrity
acid-rich formulations may still show slow leaching

element_evidence.reason: Starch is repeatedly described as OH-rich and channel-forming, supporting hydrogen-bonded proton transport.
PVA supplies complementary OH-mediated hydrogen bonding and serves as an analogous film-forming compatibiliser.
Choline chloride is directly evidenced as the complexing component of a phosphoric-acid deep eutectic proton medium.
Phosphoric acid provides the proton source and, in eutectic or confined form, is a plausible non-crystallising conducting phase.

instances.novelty_rationale: The evidence supports starch/PVA hydrogen-bonded hosts and ChCl/PA deep eutectic proton media separately, but not their explicit merger. The novelty is using a biopolymer blend to immobilise a cold-tolerant acid DES.

instances.composition_description: A chitosan membrane containing phosphoric-acid-loaded halloysite nanotubes to combine biopolymer retention with tubular nanoconfinement.
expected_properties: nanoconfinement: PA@HNT-type domains should preserve confined proton pathways
retention: both chitosan and HNTs are associated with reduced acid loss
cold_window: confined acid and bound water may remain mobile below 273 K
risk_flags: performance may depend strongly on residual humidity

element_evidence.reason: Chitosan is evidenced as a retention-capable acid-interacting host and is an appropriate analog scaffold for nanotube-filled membranes.
HNTs are directly reported to host phosphoric acid and reduce leaching through tubular confinement.
Phosphoric acid is the active proton-conducting medium and is analogously effective when retained inside nanostructured composites.

instances.novelty_rationale: This is a plausible extension from PA@HNT confinement to a chitosan-supported membrane. The novelty lies in pairing two independent retention motifs to target cold stability.

instances.composition_description: A composite membrane built from chitosan, phosphotungstic acid, and 1-D attapulgite following the reported acid-immobilised nanoconfinement motif.
expected_properties: nanoconfinement: directly supported 1-D filler–acid–polymer channel architecture
proton_relay: heteropolyacid should provide dense relay sites
retention: both scaffold and filler are reported to immobilise the acid
risk_flags: heteropolyacid hydration sensitivity may affect subzero performance
mechanical brittleness may rise at high inorganic loading

element_evidence.reason: The source directly reports chitosan as the acid-interacting scaffold in this composite motif.
PWA is directly cited as the proton-relay acid phase immobilised in the composite.
Attapulgite is directly cited as the 1-D nanoconfining filler supporting transport-channel formation and acid retention.

instances.novelty_rationale: This exact-match control is retained because it is the clearest directly evidenced fibrous nanoconfined acid scaffold in the pool. It anchors the more speculative cold-optimised variants against a known reported architecture.

instances.composition_description: A hybrid film combining protonated phosphate glass as the retained amorphous proton medium with PVA as a flexible OH-rich binder.
expected_properties: pathway_continuity: amorphous phosphate domains should avoid crystallisation-driven interruptions
hydrogen_bonding: glass OH sites plus PVA OH groups may support mixed proton-transfer modes
form_factor: PVA could mitigate brittleness of a neat glass-derived phase
risk_flags: glass-rich loading could embrittle the film

element_evidence.reason: Phosphate glass is directly evidenced as an amorphous proton-transport medium with strong hydrogen bonding and retained proton species, though stability can depend on hydration.
PVA provides an analogous OH-rich flexible binder that can interconnect inorganic proton-conducting domains without removing hydrogen-bond functionality.

instances.novelty_rationale: The novelty is hybridising an intrinsically continuous phosphate-glass proton medium with a softer polymer binder to improve low-temperature formability. The pool supports each component role but not this specific hybrid.
